**Status:** exploration. Aggregates only.

::: {.callout-warning title="The status columns are not dated"}
The instalment status and the protest status are the status at extraction. They are not the status on the enrolment date. An association between a request and later recovery is not a causal effect.
:::

## Question

What share of VAT (ICMS) certificates has an instalment request, how often a request is broken, and how does recovery differ for certificates with and without a request, a break or a protest?

## Data

The setup cell prints the window and the source. The instalment table and the protest table link to the legal-entity VAT (ICMS) extract by the debt id. Both tables cover enrolments from the start of the window. Certificates enrolled before the window stay out of these shares.

## Method

A request date or a break date outside the window is counted and left unchanged. It is not used as an event time, and an impossible break date does not close a request.

The share with a request is the number of certificates with a valid request date divided by the certificates enrolled inside the window. Recovery is the sum of GARE amounts divided by the sum of enrolled values.

The time from enrolment to the first request, from the request to a valid break, and from enrolment to a valid protest date uses the Kaplan–Meier estimator

$$\hat S(t)=\prod_{t_j\le t}\left(1-\frac{d_j}{n_j}\right)$$

The curve shows $1-\hat S(t)$. $d_j$ is the number of events in month $t_j$ and $n_j$ is the number of certificates still at risk. Certificates with no event by the end of the window are censored. A point with fewer certificates at risk than the suppression floor is hidden. Kaplan and Meier (1958) define the estimator.

*Reference:* Kaplan, E. L., & Meier, P. (1958). Nonparametric estimation from incomplete observations. *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 53(282), 457–481. https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1958.10501452

## How to read

In the share chart, the horizontal axis is the enrolment year and the vertical axis is the share of certificates with a request. Compare origins. A higher line is a higher share. It is not a recovery rate.

In a Kaplan–Meier chart, the horizontal axis is months since the start of the spell and the vertical axis is the share that has had the event. A steeper line is an earlier event. The curve is not a causal effect of the instalment or of the protest.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-date-quality
#| tbl-cap: "Impossible dates. Counted and left unchanged."
quality = pl.DataFrame([
    I.date_quality(instalments, "data_rompimento"),
    I.date_quality(protests, "data_protesto"),
])
print("Dates outside the window, and break years before year 1000, are flagged. They are not rewritten.")
I.publish(quality)
```

```{python}
#| tbl-cap: "Share of certificates with an instalment request, by enrolment year and origin."
share, n_sup = I.request_share(panel, instalments, cdas=cohort)
print(f"Cells pooled by the suppression rule: {n_sup}")
I.publish(share)
```

## What not to conclude

The tables cover enrolments inside the window. They do not describe older certificates. The status is the extraction status. A higher recovery for certificates with a request is an association. It is not the effect of granting the instalment, and it is not the effect of the protest. A payment is not the same thing as recovery of the whole credit. The comparison of amounts before and after the protest date is descriptive. The protest date is not assigned by an experiment.
